name: Query file manager
blurb: Convert your licensed spec PDFs locally and query them for verbatim excerpts — and ground the design agents on them. No vector DB; no spec text leaves this PC.

converter.label: PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)
converter.help: Only needed to convert PDFs. Large download (ML stack). The repo pins 2.123.1 — do not upgrade without revalidating retrieval accuracy. The [rapidocr] extra adds onnxruntime, which convert_pdf.py's RapidOCR fallback needs (plain docling ships rapidocr without its runtime).

tabs.title: Corpus
tabs.blurb: What this machine actually has. Run this first — it tells you which collections are queryable now and what is still missing. The OpenSees and worked-example collections ship with the module; the specifications are your own converted PDFs.

run.label: Check corpus
command:
import pathlib,sqlite3,json,sys
root=pathlib.Path(r"{data_dir}")/"grokbot"
print("workspace:", root)
std=root/"documents"/"standards"
pdfs=sorted(p.name for p in (root/"documents"/"standards").rglob("*.pdf")) if std.is_dir() else []
print()
print("== your licensed specifications ==")
print("  folder:", std)
print("  PDFs present:", len(pdfs))
for n in pdfs[:25]: print("   -", n)
conv=sorted(p.stem for p in (root/"markdown").glob("*.md")) if (root/"markdown").is_dir() else []
print("  converted stems:", ", ".join(conv[:25]) or "(none yet)")
print()
print("== search indexes ==")
for name,what in (("spec_fts.sqlite","your converted specifications"),("phase2_fts.sqlite","OpenSees docs + worked examples (ships with the module)")):
    f=root/"search"/name
    if f.is_file():
        try:
            c=sqlite3.connect(f); n=c.execute("select count(*) from chunks").fetchone()[0]
            print(f"  {name:20} {n:>7} chunks   {what}")
        except Exception as e: print(f"  {name:20} present but unreadable: {e}")
    else:
        print(f"  {name:20} MISSING           {what}")
print()
idx=root/"indexes"/"documents.json"
if idx.is_file():
    d=json.loads(idx.read_text())
    rows=d if isinstance(d,list) else list(d.values())
    cols={}
    for r in rows:
        if isinstance(r,dict): cols[r.get("collection")]=cols.get(r.get("collection"),0)+1
    print("== collections ==")
    for k,v in sorted(cols.items(), key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"  {str(k):24} {v} documents")
print()
if not (root/"search"/"spec_fts.sqlite").is_file():
    print("NEXT: the specification corpus is empty. Put your own licensed PDFs in the standards")
    print("      folder above, convert each one on the Convert PDF tab using its canonical stem,")
    print("      then run Rebuild index. Until then, query the opensees and examples collections,")
    print("      which ship with the module.")
else:
    print("Specification corpus is present. Queries default to it.")

tabs.title: Query
tabs.blurb: Verbatim excerpts from the converted corpus. `found: false` is an honest answer — nothing is paraphrased or invented. Only corpus=specification, part=standard may supply design values; OpenSees and example content is not authoritative.

fields.label: Project
fields.help: Queries are logged to this project's folder.

fields.label: Query
fields.placeholder: e.g. E3-4   ·   panel zone shear strength   ·   effective length factor

fields.label: Document
fields.help: Canonical stems, fixed by the skills — retrieval ids depend on them.

fields.label: Collection
fields.help: Specifications come from your own converted PDFs. The OpenSees and examples collections ship with the module and work before you convert anything.

fields.label: Include commentary
fields.help: Off by default: only corpus=specification, part=standard may supply design values.

tabs.title: Convert PDF
tabs.blurb: Docling at full accuracy: TableFormer ACCURATE, formula enrichment on, OCR fallback. Accuracy flags are never lowered — use page chunking if a machine runs out of memory. Needs the optional component "PDF converter (Docling 2.123.1)" — install it once from the Modules tab (large download, the ML stack); the hub refuses to run this tab until it is present.

run.label: Convert
run.crash_hint: Convert again with the same stem -- it resumes from the last finished chunk (the log shows 'Resume: reusing existing chunk pages'). If it dies at the same place twice, lower Pages per chunk (5 -> 2) or use Page range to isolate the page; a memory-hungry page in PyTorch or onnxruntime is the usual cause.

fields.label: Specification PDF
fields.help: Your own licensed copy. Nothing is uploaded anywhere — conversion runs on this machine.

fields.label: Canonical stem
fields.help: Must match exactly: the skills' id traps are edition-specific.

fields.label: Pages per chunk
fields.help: 5 is the documented default. Lower it only to work around out-of-memory, never to gain speed.

tabs.title: Re-process
tabs.blurb: Rebuild one converted document's searchable markdown, sections, equations and tables from the Docling chunks already on disk — no re-conversion, minutes not hours. Use it after a pipeline fix, or when a document's text looks like another's. Pick the stem exactly as the conversion named it (the Corpus tab lists them), and give it the source PDF (equation ids, table captions and ligature repair all read it), then run Rebuild index. The converter's records go to indexes/converted; Rebuild index reads them from there.

run.label: Re-process document
run.crash_hint: Re-processing reads the PDF only for the equation census; if it died there, run it again with the source PDF left blank.

fields.label: Converted document
fields.help: The stem the conversion used — the name of its .search.md in the markdown folder.

fields.label: Source PDF (optional)
fields.help: Only needed for the equation census. Leave empty to skip it.

tabs.title: Rebuild index
tabs.blurb: Rebuild the FTS index and slices after converting or revising documents.

tabs.title: Audit corpus
tabs.blurb: Check the built index for the faults a query cannot see: another document's text under this one's ids, a document indexed twice, commentary tagged as provisions, equation LaTeX printed with another id, a table of contents posing as a numbered table, split ligatures, watermarks, missing headings. Rebuild index runs this automatically; run it here after converting or re-processing, and read indexes/audit_report.md. What to do about each finding: skills/CHECK-AND-CLEAN-CONVERSIONS.md.

fields.label: Folder with the source PDFs (optional)
fields.help: Absolute path of the folder holding the source PDFs (the project folder you converted from). Lets the audit count the equation ids printed in each PDF and compare them with the index. Leave empty to skip that check.

tabs.title: Retrieval plan
tabs.blurb: Run a whole wave-1 plan at once — the batch path the SNL skill uses to fill hinge parameters.

fields.label: Plan JSON
fields.help: {plan_id, submitted, queries:[{qid, doc, type, query, purpose, want_commentary, context_neighbors}]}

tabs.title: Grounding
tabs.blurb: What the design agents are asking this corpus, and what they got back. HR Steel and CFS point their standards search here automatically.
